column1: # fresh-checks.tsv (harbor#1287) — the generated files bin/doc-fresh-verify.sh proves current, each in seconds.
# file <TAB> check (sh, run from the repo root; exit 0 fresh, 1 stale, anything else unchecked) <TAB> fix <TAB> needs
# THE HEADER (harbor#1434). Every file named here carries one comment line `generated-by: <command>` in its first 20 lines, <command> equal to its `fix` column;
# bin/doc-shape.sh holds the two equal both ways (doc.fresh-registered), so a generated file with no row, or a row whose file lacks the header, is red.
# `needs` is the path that must exist for the row to apply (default: the file itself) — an exported tree carries no
# dev layer, and a row with nothing to judge is SKIPPED, never red. A `-` row names a script that has a --check mode
# and is NOT a generated-file freshness check, with the reason: tests/doc/fresh-verify/fresh-verify.test.sh fails on any bin/ script
# with a --check mode that talks about staleness and is in neither list, so a new generator must be decided here.
